items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1972-06-26
items.q: Faith Marvel and then taught Louis to read.

ctx.x: Well, my teacher used to say the Green Book was the one that you played by ear. But I don't know. I don't know, man. They had some of them.

That's how I knew Louis could read. You know, he's talking about reading. When Louis was on the boat with Faith Marvel. And Louis was on the boat for about three or four years. Faith Marvel and then taught Louis to read. I was amazed when Louis came off that boat. He came around and taught him, and he was playing with us. We got in that Red Book, man. And didn't miss a note. That's a tough book. Yeah, man.
And you knew him before? Faith was the one who taught him?

items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1967-02-09
items.q: Louis was on the boat with Fade Marble.

ctx.x: There are a lot of different theories as to why King Oliver asked Louis to join him. A lot of people say that he was scared of Louis, and that he thought that if he had Louis in his own band, he wouldn't be cut. Do you think this is true?

No, I don't think it's true at all. You hear all kinds of funny rumors later on about jazz musicians. King Oliver sent for Louis because it was the Spentonese band. He wanted to change to get out of this New Orleans six-piece deals. He wanted to build his band up to what he did, to an eight or nine-piece band. It gets sort of modern-ish at the time, you know, with reeds. And Louis was the greatest thing in New Orleans when he sent for Louis. He wasn't doing Louis a favor. Louis was on the boat with Fade Marble.…

You were talking about Armstrong, Albert. Yeah. And remember you saying the other day that you thought that Louis got a lot from Bunk and those more recent records made in American music by Bunk, you didn't feel were really Bunk in his prime. Obviously they weren't because he was getting on years. Could you tell us a bit about Bunk? You heard Bunk in New Orleans.
